title: PUMP (master compressor)
author: Robbie (master page plumbing adapted from Tone+FX by Digital Alchemy DSP; SETTINGS row adapted from digihealth by irpina)
description: PUMP, an SP-303 Vinyl Sim-style levelling compressor on everything the Digitone plays, with its own master page (FUNC+LFO, then LEFT/RIGHT to the page after the stock ones). A = on/off; B = ATK: punch, each hit's front gets through before the gain comes down; C = OUT: output level before the ceiling, -32 to +6 dB, for headroom; D = RAT: the ratio, AUTO (set by CMP), 2:1 to 20:1 or LIMIT; E = CMP: threshold, ratio and automatic make-up together, so more is always louder and denser; F = REL: release from LEVEL (slow levelling) through GLUE to PUMP (fast, breathing); G = WRM: soft saturation; H = MIX: parallel blend. The page: a record that turns with the tempo, a tonearm that rides in with the gain reduction, the eight controls with values and a gain-reduction meter; YES swaps the record for a graph of the last 2.8 s of gain reduction; SETTINGS > PUMP ANIMATION turns the animation off (~1% less CPU), saved with the project. Always on: a 30 Hz high-pass in the compressor's detector, so inaudible sub-bass does not eat into the pump (the output keeps it). Press and turn a knob for big steps. Settings are stored per pattern. Off it costs nothing; on, a few percent of the processor (more with WRM). It runs as core-dn1 4.0's insert audio, so it is on every output: main outs, headphones and USB. Its own output ceiling keeps the make-up gain from clipping. Standalone: not with Tone+FX, which owns the same master page hook.
